result.summary: Backport PR #35168 to the 31.x release branch. It ensures LoadBlockIndex checks for BLOCK_HAVE_DATA before adding blocks to m_blocks_unlinked on node startup, and includes a functional regression test.
result.problem: In v31.1, LoadBlockIndex inserts blocks into m_blocks_unlinked based on nTx > 0 without checking whether the block data is actually on disk. For pruned blocks whose parents are header-only, this causes the CheckBlockIndex invariant (!foundInUnlinked) to fail assertions on startup or during block connection, crashing nodes running with -checkblockindex (such as regtest functional tests).
evidence: Author notes the regression test feature_prune_stale_fork.py fails against the v31.1 release binary on the assertion and passes on this branch
result.scope_notes: Clean cherry-pick backport of two commits from master with minor test_runner.py context adjustment.
result.card: This PR backports PR #35168 to the 31.x release branch, fixing a validation assertion failure on startup. When running with -checkblockindex (default on regtest), nodes with pruned stale-fork blocks crash due to LoadBlockIndex adding blocks without block data to m_blocks_unlinked. The fix ensures BLOCK_HAVE_DATA is present before insertion and includes a dedicated functional test.

risk.why: A flaw in block index reconstruction during startup could corrupt internal tracking of unlinked blocks or prevent proper chain synchronization.
